config.title: Undo/Redo

intro.title: Undo/Redo
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple text editor that allows you to undo and redo your changes. You will learn how to manage application state by storing a history of user actions. The core programming concept is the Command Pattern, which you'll implement using arrays to track past and future states. You'll use Angular components, TypeScript arrays, and event handling to create this feature. By the end, you'll have a working editor where you can type text and navigate through your edit history with undo and redo buttons.
intro.usecase: The undo/redo pattern is essential in any interactive application where users need to correct mistakes or explore different states without fear of permanent errors. You'll see this in text editors like Google Docs, where users can revert formatting changes, in design tools like Figma for adjusting element properties, and in complex form-based dashboards where administrators might modify multiple data filters or settings. As an Angular developer, implementing this pattern allows you to build more professional, user-friendly interfaces that handle state changes predictably and safely.

objectives: Implement a service to manage undo/redo state using Angular's dependency injection
Construct a command pattern to track user actions in a TypeScript array
Initialize component state with the undo/redo service to maintain action history
Bind UI controls to service methods for undo and redo operations
Configure event handlers to capture user interactions that modify application state
Update component templates to reflect the current state of the undo/redo history
Integrate undo/redo functionality into a sample Angular application component

steps.title: Import Component and CommonModule from @angular/core and @angular/common
steps.instruction: Import Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common' to set up the Angular component for the Undo/Redo lesson.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by the symbol name and the module path. You'll need both imports for this lesson.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component file will have the necessary Angular imports to create a component and use Angular directives.
successCriteria: Component is imported from '@angular/core' and CommonModule is imported from '@angular/common'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some of the required modules. Make sure to import both Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the main component class with @Component decorator
steps.instruction:
Create a class named UndoRedoComponent and decorate it with @Component, setting selector to 'app-undo-redo' and template to a placeholder like '

Undo/Redo Component

'.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' that you imported earlier. Define the selector and template properties.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, CommonModule } from '@angular/core';

// Create the UndoRedoComponent class with @Component decorator here
steps.expectedOutcome: A component class is defined with the correct decorator and basic configuration.
successCriteria: UndoRedoComponent class is created with @Component decorator, selector set to 'app-undo-redo', and template contains a placeholder paragraph.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have the @Component decorator with selector 'app-undo-redo' and a template with a paragraph.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class isn't properly defined. Check that you used @Component with the correct selector and template.

steps.title: Initialize state arrays for history, current index, and current value
steps.instruction: Inside the UndoRedoComponent class, define three properties: history (string array), currentIndex (number), and currentValue (string). Initialize history as an empty array, currentIndex as 0, and currentValue as an empty string.
steps.hint: Add these properties directly in the component class body with appropriate TypeScript types and initial values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class will have three typed properties initialized with default values to track undo/redo state.
successCriteria: Component has history: string[] = [], currentIndex: number = 0, and currentValue: string = '' properties defined.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some properties, but make sure all three are present with correct types and initial values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component is missing the required state properties. Check that you've defined history, currentIndex, and currentValue with proper TypeScript types and initial values.

steps.title: Define a method to update the current value and add to history
steps.instruction: Inside the UndoRedoComponent class, create a method named updateValue that takes a new string value as a parameter, updates currentValue, adds it to the history array, and increments currentIndex.
steps.hint: Remember to push the new value to the history array and update both currentValue and currentIndex properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has an updateValue method that manages state updates and maintains history tracking.
successCriteria: The updateValue method is defined with a string parameter, updates currentValue, pushes to history array, and sets currentIndex to the last position.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the method, but check that it properly updates currentValue, adds to history array, and adjusts currentIndex.
steps.feedbackWrong: The updateValue method is missing or doesn't follow the required structure. Review the method signature and implementation.

steps.title: Add a text input field bound to currentValue
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add an HTML input element of type 'text' and use Angular's two-way data binding [(ngModel)] to bind it to the currentValue property.
steps.hint: Use the ngModel directive from FormsModule. The syntax is [(ngModel)]="currentValue".
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example: binding an input to a property -->
<input type="text" [(ngModel)]="userName" />
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will contain an input field that is two-way bound to the currentValue property, allowing the user to type and see changes reflected immediately.
successCriteria: The template includes an input element with type="text" and [(ngModel)]="currentValue".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an input, but it's missing the two-way binding. Make sure to use [(ngModel)]="currentValue".
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element or its binding is not correctly implemented. Check that you have type="text" and [(ngModel)]="currentValue".

steps.title: Add a button to trigger value updates and wire it to updateValue
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add a button element with the label 'Update' and wire its click event to call the updateValue method with the currentValue property as the argument.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax (click)="updateValue(currentValue)" on the button element.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler in Angular template
<button (click)="saveData(data)">Save</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template should contain a button labeled 'Update' that when clicked will trigger the updateValue method with the current input value.
successCriteria: A button element with the text 'Update' is present in the template, and its click event is bound to updateValue(currentValue).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but check if it has the correct label 'Update' and if the click event properly calls updateValue(currentValue).
steps.feedbackWrong: The button element with the click handler is missing or incorrect. Make sure to add <button (click)="updateValue(currentValue)">Update</button> in the template.

steps.title: Add undo and redo buttons and wire them to their methods
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add two <button> elements: one labeled 'Undo' and one labeled 'Redo'. Wire their (click) events to the undo() and redo() methods respectively.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax: (click)="methodName()" on each button.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will contain two functional buttons that trigger the undo and redo logic when clicked.
successCriteria: Two buttons with labels 'Undo' and 'Redo' are present in the template, each with correct (click) event bindings to the respective methods.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added buttons, but check the labels or event bindings. Ensure 'Undo' button uses (click)="undo()" and 'Redo' uses (click)="redo()".
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons are missing or incorrectly configured. Add two <button> elements with labels and (click) event bindings as instructed.

steps.title: Display the current value and history index in the template
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add two paragraph elements to display the current value and current index using interpolation.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to bind component properties in the template. Display currentValue and currentIndex.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show the current value and index values that update when you interact with the component.
successCriteria: Two paragraph elements are added to the template using interpolation to display currentValue and currentIndex.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some display elements, but make sure you have both paragraphs showing currentValue and currentIndex.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet display the current value and index. Add two paragraph elements with interpolation.

steps.title: Disable undo/redo buttons when at history limits
steps.instruction: Add [disabled] bindings to the undo and redo buttons that check if currentIndex is at the start or end of the history array.
steps.hint: Use property binding syntax [disabled]="condition". For undo, disable when currentIndex is 0 or less. For redo, disable when currentIndex is at the last index of history.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: disabling a button based on condition
<button [disabled]="isDisabled">Save</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The undo button should be disabled when there are no previous states to undo, and the redo button should be disabled when there are no future states to redo.
successCriteria: Both undo and redo buttons have [disabled] bindings that correctly evaluate based on currentIndex and history length.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some disabling logic, but check both buttons. The undo button should be disabled when currentIndex <= 0, and redo when currentIndex >= history.length - 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons are not properly disabled at the history limits. Review how to bind the [disabled] property to conditions using currentIndex and history length.
